P1.evidence: No setter suffix on this call and no setter call referenced — the prospect came off a YouTube video and a form — so the read-back check does not apply. The frame ran three parts of four: 'where are you today? Where do you want to be? we can help, I can show you one of the many options that we have' — no 'what's in the way' and no 'what you need'. Agreement was sought loosely at the top ('Just dive into it, if that's cool with yourself') rather than against the frame. The open question was clean: 'I'll leave the floor to you, Brad. How can we potentially help?'

P2.evidence: Work was asked and answered well — 'What do you do for work if you don't want me to ask you?' — producing agricultural sales, the pastorate and four kids. Age was never asked; 44 fell out of a story. No height, no weight. The injury was volunteered, but the rep did then probe it properly ('When, when was this injury?', 'And since September, have you been working out? What have you been doing?'), which is the one piece of real baseline work on the call. Everything else was skipped, and one omission is serious: the prospect disclosed raised blood sugar and a medication decision, and no health-conditions question ever followed. No diet question despite the disclosure being dietary, no sleep, no energy.

P3.evidence: The strongest discovery in the batch. The strength-or-mobility fork was put directly ('That gets you the strength, or is it the mobility for you too?'), then sharpened into durability versus potential ('is the wider goal for yourself, Brad, to become more durable in your body, or is it to realize your physical potential? There's a difference'). The mirror question did the real work — 'When you look yourself in the mirror a year from now, who do you want to see back, mainly in the eyes?' — and produced the spiritual-physical identity gap the whole call turned on. Family impact ran through to grandkids and hiking. The tangible probe surfaced the bodyfat target and the blood sugar. Only the physical-thing-you-cannot-do-now question and the reflect-back were soft.

P4.evidence: 'Why are we having this conversation today, Brad, as opposed to, I don't know, in December?' is a good adjacent probe and produced 'I've had a couple conversations with people, I just haven't found the right fit'. 'What are you looking for? How do you like to be supported?' let him name structure and guidance as the gap. But the actual sequence never ran: no what-have-you-tried on training, no what-happened, no why-didn't-it-stick, no single-obstacle question. The prospect asked the root-cause question of himself — 'why haven't I figured this out?' — and the rep did not pick it up, which was the open door on this call.

P5.evidence: Third call in three with no consequence frame at all, and the costliest instance. The prospect built the frame himself and handed it over — 'all this stuff is staring me in the face going, okay, the longer you wait, the more you're making the, I would say the lazy decision' — with a medication fork sitting behind it. The response was 'Okay. Okay. Okay. Yep, yep' and a pivot to the want-or-need question. Nothing about what two more years looks like, nothing about whether he is willing to settle, no line in the sand. When the price landed a few minutes later there was no accumulated cost of inaction for it to sit against.

P6.evidence: The belief question ran properly and in the right place, before price: 'alignment is obviously important for us. Do you feel like what I've actually shown you, you have the trust in Trevor and us to actually help you with your goals?'. The all-in question never came. And P6c was inverted — the answer to the alignment question was not a yes at all, it was a pre-emptive price objection about coaches who deliver 'some stupid, ridiculous number'. The playbook says return to Phase 5 on hesitation; the rep instead said 'brace yourself' and read the numbers out.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted — both tiers presented, 12 months recommended, 'In this moment, which one are you like kind of leaning towards?' — and nothing followed. No payment, no Trevor booking, no agreement, no onboarding instructions. The downsell was not closed either: it ended on 'give me some time to chew on it' with no link sent, no follow-up call and no next contact owned by the rep.

objection_plays.detail: The clearest money trigger in the batch and not one scripted move ran. No isolation ('finances aside, nothing else keeping you from 100%?'), no SHOULD-versus-HOW reframe, no 'most clients pay upfront, but for some we break it up — want to explore making it work?', no permission question, and none of the six financial-picture items: cash on hand, monthly surplus, number of cards, available credit, used versus available, investments. The only probe was 'You don't think or?', and on the answer the rep left the offer entirely. This is a capability question rather than a knowledge one — the same rep ran most of the financial-picture sequence with Nick Hartas the day before, on a prospect who was far less able to pay.

Triggered on the downsell — 'just give me some time to chew on it, and I'm going to hold for right now'. None of the play ran: no 'do you feel what we've gone through can get you to your goal', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is'. The call ended thirty seconds later.

Two script gaps in one exchange. First, there is no play for a hard budget ceiling declared before the number is spoken — OC assumes an openable wallet, and this prospect pre-announced that every previous conversation died at the number. Second, and more consequential, there is no governance at all around descending to Primal University: the rep introduced a $200/month product on his own initiative, priced it live, and coached the prospect on how to extract value from it in one month and cancel. Nothing in the playbook says when a downsell is permitted, what it costs, or how it should be framed.

notes: Discovery here was the best of the batch and the close was the worst — the rep built genuine emotional alignment, skipped the consequence frame entirely, then abandoned the offer within seconds of the first money objection rather than running any part of OC. Coach the sequence: no consequence frame means no price tolerance, and a stated 'I can't spend $6,000' is where the money play starts, not where the call ends.
